Ashwin vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:50844) on 11
December, 2024
Author: Kuldeep Mathur

Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2024:RJ-JD:50844]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 15374/2024 Ashwin S/o Chimanlal, Aged About 21 Years, R/o Dalar, P.s.
Sallopat Dist Banswara (Raj.)
(Presently Lodged In Jail Banswara)

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Raghuveer Singh Bhati
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Urja Ram Kalbi, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 11/12/2024 1.

This application for bail under Section 483 BNSS (439 Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.78/2024, registered at Police Station Sallopat,
District Banswara, for offences under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of IPC; Sections 5(l)/6 of POCSO Act; and Section 84 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Drawing attention of the Court towards the statements of the victim- 'P' recorded before the competent criminal Court as PW.1, learned counsel submitted that the victim- 'P' during her Court statements has not supported the prosecution story and has turned hostile.

Learned counsel submitted that since the victim- 'P' during her Court statements has not supported the prosecution [2024:RJ-JD:50844] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-15374/2024] story, the chances of the petitioner's conviction in the present case are very bleak.

3. Learned counsel submitted that the other material prosecution witnesses of the case namely Laxman (PW.2) and Smt. Sushila (PW.3) have also not supported the prosecution story and have turned hostile.

Ashwin vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:50844) on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195606567/
1 4.

Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused- petitioner.
5. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application.

However, he was not in a position to refute the fact that the victim 'P' and the other material prosecution witnesses of the case during their Court statements have not supported the prosecution story and have turned hostile.
6. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

7. Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
8. Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 BNSS (439 Cr.P.C.) is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner- Ashwin S/o Chimanlal arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.78/2024,
registered at Police Station Sallopat, District Banswara, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and [2024:RJ-JD:50844] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-15374/2024] two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
9. It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 154-himanshu/-
